title: People have real hair, moustaches and wet eyes
items: Up close, a person's hair is no longer one smooth cap: strands are grown over it at load, combed by the cut of their year, with broken edges and a sheen along the strands.
Hans the 1904 coachman wears a short back and sides and a full moustache; Otis Bardwell in 1835 wears his hair brushed forward with side whiskers. Both are reconstructed choices, listed in Liberties.
Hair stays under a hat: nothing shows through Hans's top hat.
Eyes catch a small sharp highlight on a domed cornea, and the whites are shaded toward the corners.
